Subject: Horizon - sudden 5xx/429s after model v3.2 rollout

Hi Aditya,

We pushed your v3.2 model yesterday evening (UTC) and started seeing an immediate uptick in 500s and 429s across our inference traffic. Symptoms: elevated 5xx (~2.8% -> 12%), repeated client retries, and timeouts reported by downstream services. Latency P95 went from ~120ms to ~1.2s.

This is customer-facing (multiple teams impacted). I attached a small sample of logs and our service metrics. Can you please confirm whether Redwood made any kernel/quant changes in that rollout? We need an ETA for mitigation and any immediate rollback option.

Attachments:
- horizon_error_log_20260722.zip (errors + stack traces)
- service-metrics-2026-07-22.csv

Thanks,
Timothy Nguyen

Subject: Re: Horizon - sudden 5xx/429s after model v3.2 rollout

Quick update from model side: v3.2 included a new quantization profile targeting 4-bit kernels and a small kernel selection tweak for long prompts. We did not expect functional regressions, but the telemetry shows increased tail latency for A100 hosts in the pool we use for Horizon (see attached quant-profile-diff.txt).

Preliminary hypothesis: the new quant profile reduces numerical headroom for certain token sequences -> longer decode steps for a subset of requests. That increases per-request latency which in turn causes client retries and 429s at the edge.

Immediate actions I recommend:
- Rollback quant profile for Horizon deployment to the previous profile (v3.1 quant).
- Route Horizon production traffic to the v3.1-safe variant (edge routing flip).
- Collect a stratified sample of requests that hit >800ms to isolate token patterns.

I've attached the diff and a short metric export. If Jonas can put a temporary throttle on client retry windows we should be able to stop the retry storm.

Attachments:
- quant-profile-diff.txt

Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 22, 2026 at 10:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Preliminary hypothesis: the new quant profile reduces numerical headroom for certain token sequences -> longer decode steps for a subset of requests. That increases per-request latency which in turn causes client retries and 429s at the edge.

I've validated the spike in our infra metrics. Key points:
- Instance-level tail latency (A100 pool #7) jumped at 2026-07-22T01:45Z coincident with the v3.2 canary.
- Autoscaler reacted but pods are congesting because of long-running inferences and KV cache pressure.
- Edge service is returning 429s when per-route concurrency limits are reached; downstream clients are retrying aggressively (client TTL 500ms).

Immediate mitigation executed (10:12 PDT):
- Rolled routing for Horizon to v3.1-safe (edge flip).
- Increased per-route concurrency cap for Horizon by +20% as a temporary measure.
- Opened PagerDuty incident PDR-12934.

Next steps:
- Marissa: confirm rollback of quant profile in serving config.
- I'll push a KV cache warm-up and a temporary backoff policy at the edge to reduce retries.

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Horizon - post-rollout 5xx/429 surge and timeouts (RCA + next steps)

Tim —

Appreciate the patience and for sending logs. Summary and next steps:

Summary:
- Root cause: regression introduced by the v3.2 quantization profile that increased decode time for a subset of token patterns on our A100 serving pool. That increase pushed request durations into the region where client-side retries and our edge concurrency limits produced amplified 429/500s.
- Mitigation performed: we routed Horizon to v3.1-safe (2026-07-22T10:12 PDT), increased concurrency cap, and applied a temporary edge backoff. Errors returned to baseline within ~30 minutes.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD tomorrow:
- Full RCA doc (including request samples and infra traces) — link will be emailed.
- Action items: blocking the v3.2 quant profile for Horizon until compatibility tests are added to the rollout gate; adjust autoscaler heuristics for similar workloads; implement automatic client backoff guidance in SDK.
- Compensation: I will escalate your credit request to our finance team and provide a proposed credit within 24 hours.

For Redwood execs: we should consider adding a pre-rollout canary that includes a quant-stress test for customer slices with aggressive retry clients.

Aditya Rao
